tasks.note: Mission-conditioned task registry. Tolerances are declared engineering tolerances (assumptions), not measured error bars; the evaluation varies them by x0.5 and x2. Status thresholds are expressed in tolerance units: match = exp(-z^2/2), so 0.6065 is z = 1 tolerance and 0.1353 is z = 2 tolerances.

order: SITE_CONSTRAINT: a hard site constraint fails -> NON_TRANSFERABLE (the site cannot host the operation).
PHYSICS_PRIMARY: a primary physical dependency is not reproducible in the field and has no correction model -> NON_TRANSFERABLE.
EVIDENCE: available factor weight fraction below the task's min_evidence -> UNKNOWN.

SUPPORTED: lower bootstrap bound of the task match >= 1-tolerance threshold, evidence quality >= supported_min_quality, primary-factor resolution sufficient, and no primary physics dependency that is only partially reproducible or model-corrected.
CONDITIONAL: point match >= 2-tolerance threshold but a caveat applies (CI below threshold, low evidence quality, insufficient resolution, or a partial/model-corrected primary physics dependency).
WEAK: point match below the 2-tolerance threshold.
Secondary physics dependencies never change the status; they are listed as certificate limitations and red-team findings.

tasks.name: DEM-based hazard mapping rehearsal
tasks.description: Rehearse slope/roughness hazard mapping and avoidance planning from orbital-class DEMs.
limitations: Lander-scale (metre) hazards such as boulders are not resolved by any input DEM.

tasks.name: Rover route planning and autonomous navigation
tasks.description: Exercise route planners and autonomy on terrain geometry statistically similar to the target region.
limitations: Traversability thresholds depend on wheel-soil behaviour, which is not transferred by terrain geometry.

tasks.name: Wheel-soil traction and sinkage qualification
tasks.description: Qualify wheel traction, sinkage and drawbar pull.
limitations: Field soils are unmeasured; reduced-gravity soil strength effects are empirically documented and not reproduced at 1 g.

tasks.name: EVA field-geology traverse training
tasks.description: Train crews and science teams on geological traverses and observation planning.
limitations: Suit mobility under reduced gravity and pressurisation is not reproduced.

tasks.name: Geological sampling protocol rehearsal
tasks.description: Rehearse sample selection, documentation and handling protocols.
limitations: Mineralogy and lithology are not inferred from DEMs.

tasks.name: Solar array siting and energy-constrained scheduling
tasks.description: Plan array placement and operations against solar geometry and available irradiance.
limitations: No terrain horizon shadowing at the Earth sites; panel temperature and dust deposition not modelled.

tasks.name: Low-Sun crew and robotic operations
tasks.description: Rehearse perception and operations under long, low-angle shadows.
limitations: Natural Earth low-Sun windows are seasonal and short compared with lunar polar illumination.

tasks.name: Line-of-sight and communications geometry planning
tasks.description: Plan line-of-sight between assets and relay placement over terrain.
limitations: Direct-to-Earth and relay-orbiter geometry is not reproduced by terrestrial sites.

tasks.name: Habitat and landing-pad site layout
tasks.description: Lay out habitat, pad and keep-out zones against flat-terrain availability and thermal environment.
limitations: Radiation shielding and thermal design are outside field-analog scope.

tasks.name: Excavation and regolith ISRU operations
tasks.description: Excavate, haul and process regolith; prospect volatiles.
limitations: Excavation forces scale with gravity and soil strength; volatile behaviour requires cryo-vacuum testing.

tasks.name: Dust mitigation and contamination control
tasks.description: Test dust tolerance of mechanisms, seals and optics.
limitations: Lunar electrostatic dust and low-pressure Martian aeolian transport are not reproduced outdoors on Earth.

tasks.name: Cold, dry surface operations
tasks.description: Operate equipment in persistently cold and arid surface conditions.
limitations: Earth and target temperatures/precipitation were not acquired.

evidence.statement: Proposes Earth testing with identical mass rather than identical normal load to predict extraterrestrial rigid-wheel sinkage and compaction resistance.

Parabolic-flight wheel tests on a Mars simulant reported reduced traction and increased sinkage in reduced gravity relative to 1 g at equal wheel load (as summarised in the session literature search; full text not read).
1/6 g parabolic-flight cone penetration in GRC-1 reported a markedly reduced cone index gradient (reduced shear strength), i.e. soil strength depends on gravity.

measurements.instrument: Published geologic maps of the target region
measurements.limitations: Map units may not match terrestrial process vocabulary.

measurements.name: High-resolution terrain survey
measurements.instrument: Drone photogrammetry or lidar (Earth); HiRISE DTM or LOLA 5 m products (targets)

measurements.instrument: Bevameter / shear annulus
measurements.expected_evidence: Bekker kc, kphi, n and Mohr-Coulomb c, phi for the field soil
measurements.limitations: Calibrates the counterfactual model; does not make 1 g soil behave like reduced-gravity regolith.

measurements.limitations: Does not change solar geometry; changes usable windows.

context.note: Dominant geological process tags. Grade A = peer-reviewed source checked in this session; B = authoritative non-peer-reviewed record already in EGIZ references; C = non-academic secondary source checked in this session; D = derived from the window name or general knowledge, NOT verified. Grades C and D are hypotheses for the field-research planner to verify.

compatibility.rule: 1.0 if any process tag is shared; otherwise 0.2 (morphology may still be useful but formation process differs). Declared judgment, varied in sensitivity analysis.

soil.name: Apollo-era lunar soil design estimate (rough; NASA Lunar Surface Data Book)

equations: l = sqrt(D z0);  H = b l c + W tan(phi)
slope limit: H - R_c - W tan(theta)... solved by bisection on N(H - R_c) = m g sin(theta)
findings: Within the Bekker model, a load-matched Earth test reproduces the target sinkage exactly (ratio 1.000) because soil self-weight does not appear in the model.
A mass-matched Earth test sinks 3.32x deeper than the target-gravity prediction and its slope limit differs by -3.3 deg.

The model predicts a higher traction-limited slope at target gravity than in a mass-matched Earth test. Reduced-gravity experiments report lower soil strength and traction at reduced gravity, which this model cannot represent: the direction of the transfer error is CONTESTED.
limitations: Soil parameters are rough Apollo-era lunar estimates applied to both cases; Jezero and all Earth field soils are unmeasured.
No gravity-dependent soil strength, slip-sinkage, grousers, dynamic loading or multi-pass effects.
Static, quasi-steady, equal wheel loads on a uniform slope; not a mission performance prediction.

evaluation.protocol: Deterministic; all experiments on the measured pilot bundle. Criteria pre-declared in ATLAS_PI_SCIENTIFIC_HYPOTHESES.md.

hypotheses.criterion: >= half of assessable tasks have a different top site or Kendall tau < 0.7 vs the general similarity ranking
hypotheses.caveat: Partly expected by construction (task factor sets differ from the general factor set); the measured content is how often the practical recommendation changes on real sites.

hypotheses.criterion: Optimised portfolio covers more requirements (status + LCB rule, a metric it does not optimise) than both the top-K individual and top-K general-similarity portfolios in >= 1 mission/K and fewer in none
hypotheses.caveat: On its own objective J the exact optimiser cannot lose to any baseline; only the independent coverage count is evidence.

hypotheses.criterion: Comparing an Earth slope distribution at a different baseline than the target changes the top-3 set, flips a site across the 2 deg tolerance, or shifts W1 by >= 25% of the between-site SD
hypotheses.data: terrain_evidence.json slope histograms (100 m and 400 m baselines; binned W1)

hypotheses.criterion: Explicit physical-mismatch modelling changes the status of >= 1 cell and exposes >= 1 cell whose terrain match alone would look strong
hypotheses.caveat: Status changes follow from the declared physics rules by design; the empirical content is that real sites with strong terrain matches (e.g. WHEEL_SOIL) would be recommended by a similarity-only system.

hypotheses.criterion: >= 1 measurement with EVPI >= 5% of current expected value and decision-change probability >= 20%; negative control (bevameter cannot change field statuses) must have EVPI = 0

hypotheses.reason: No defensible labels exist (11 windows, no independent analog-validity ground truth), no deep-learning framework is installed, and a learned embedding trained on 11 regional grids would be evaluated on spatially autocorrelated patches of the same windows. The deterministic descriptors are retained; see ATLAS_PI_MODEL_CARD.md.

controls.description: Water-dominated Kazakhstan window (WorldCover water 0.96) must be excluded everywhere
Spatially scrambled target grids (elevation histogram kept, terrain structure destroyed) must not yield SUPPORTED terrain transfers
Positive control: a site compared with itself (independent bootstrap seed, Mars physics) must give near-perfect terrain match and SUPPORTED route planning

method.level1: GLO-90 tiles read at 300x300 (average, COG overviews); 0.25 deg blocks; coarse slope W1 vs target 400 m slope distribution (tolerance 2 deg); blocks with >60% slopes < 0.3 deg flagged
method.level2: GLO-30 22 km windows -> 200 m local UTM grids (same functions as mission_terrain) -> ATLAS-Pi tensor

clustering.note: Exploratory Ward clustering and median/MAD outlier scores; not a validated classification.

method.novelty: Great-circle distance to EGIZ catalog windows; <15 km existing, <40 km new characterisation, else new computational candidate. Published-literature novelty was not checked for every block.

provenance.level1: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 Public (copernicus-dem-90m AWS registry)
provenance.level2: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public (copernicus-dem-30m AWS registry)

screen_agreement.note: Level-1 coarse match uses one ~370 m slope distribution; Level 2 uses multi-scale slope, traversability, roughness and relief with bootstrap. Disagreement is expected and is why Level 1 is only a screen.

limitations: Regional pilot, not a global search.
Level 1 uses GLO-90 at ~370 m and is a screen only.
Land cover, water and built fractions were not acquired: site constraints are unknown, not passed.
Discovery categories are computational; no candidate is a confirmed analog.

# Planetary Transferability Dossier — Death Valley regional window → Jezero / Perseverance landing site

Engine `atlas-pi-1.0.0` · bundle content SHA-256 `314fe48950a8b133…` · synthetic: False

## Research question

Which mission operations planned for **Jezero / Perseverance landing site** can be rehearsed at **Death Valley regional window** (United States, 36.240, -116.820), under what corrections, with what uncertainty?

## Methods

Measured 200 m terrain grids are compared at 200/400/800 m cells (Wasserstein-1 between slope and roughness distributions, relief and traversable fraction), with a 4 km spatial block bootstrap (200 replicates) for 90% intervals. Factor matches use exp(-z²/2) in declared tolerance units; statuses follow the documented rules (similarity, evidence coverage, evidence quality, resolution and physics kept separate).

## Operational Transferability (per task)

| Task | Status | Task match (90% CI) | Evidence coverage | Evidence quality | Reasons |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COLD_DRY_SURFACE | **UNKNOWN** | 1.00 (partial) (1.00–1.00) | 17% | 0.50 | EVIDENCE |
| COMMS_VISIBILITY | **WEAK** | 0.00 (0.00–0.01) | 100% | 0.90 | LOW_MATCH |
| DUST_MITIGATION | **NON_TRANSFERABLE** | 1.00 (1.00–1.00) | 100% | 0.50 | PHYSICS_PRIMARY |

## Physical mismatch (non-transferable factors)
